implementation_notes: C# has no operator overloading, so the idiomatic instance is a static class holding Combine and Identity plus a static Fold, with the carrier type as a readonly struct for value semantics and a monotonic sequence number added to break ties. string and Span<char> concatenate via string.Concat, which the standard library already implements as an associative combine - but building a large string by repeated += in a loop is quadratic in older runtimes and should use a StringBuilder or a span-based fold. Value types make the aggregate allocation-free, which is the main reason to prefer a struct instance here.
idiom_name: static Combine/Identity/Fold on a readonly struct carrier
pitfalls: LINQ's Aggregate throws on an empty sequence unless a seed is supplied - and the seed must be the identity, not default(T), which for a struct is usually not the identity.
Repeated string concatenation in a loop allocates a new string each time; use a StringBuilder or fold over spans.
A mutable struct carrier breaks value semantics and silently makes associativity depend on evaluation order.
record struct's generated equality is by value, so an instance used as a dictionary key behaves differently from a class instance.
